29.28351,-96.62838: Site of Provident City. Founded in 1909 by the Provident Land Company of Kansas City, Missouri, Provident City was the site of an early land promotion venture. 29.37979,-96.79192: Vienna (Cheney Settlement). The community of Vienna has roots that reach back to the Republic of Texas. 29.44708,-96.93405: St. James' Episcopal Church. The community of Hallettsville began in 1836, when Margaret Hallett donated land for the townsite. 29.44765,-96.93705: St. Peter Lutheran Church. The history of Lutheran ministry in the Hallettsville area can be traced to 1868, when the Rev. 29.44766,-96.93892: First Baptist Church of Hallettsville. According to local oral tradition, Baptists in Hallettsville began worshiping together about 1851. 29.44828,-96.93556: Hallettsville Public Schools. The existence of schools in Hallettsville can be traced to the early 1850s. 29.44837,-96.93559: First Methodist Church of Hallettsville. Methodist circuit riders under the stewardship of John W. DeVilbiss and Henderson D. Palmer served this area as early as 1842. 29.4494,-96.99789: St. Mary's Parish. 29.4506,-96.9976: Arthur Henry Vollentine. Arthur Henry Vollentine was born in New Jersey or Virginia about 1807. 29.45154,-96.92391: City Cemetery. On July 19, 1889, the Hallettsville town council met to discuss the poor condition of various small cemeteries in the city. 29.49618,-96.84877: Vsetin Cemetery. About 1865, newly arrived Czechoslovakian immigrants settled in this vicinity, named Sublime by earlier Irish immigrants.
